name: Lip filler

image.caption: Under the eye and lip fillers, botox in masseters

lead: Lip filler is the injection of a gel, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), to add lip volume, define the border or balance the upper and lower lip. It is one of the most widely performed non-surgical cosmetic treatments, and randomised multicentre trials have compared HA lip products head to head.

HA gels bind water and add volume where injected, and reviews call HA the gold standard lip filler because it is biocompatible and reversible. Fat transfer, collagen and permanent fillers are other methods with different durations. Some forum posters argue that mouth width matters more than fullness and that filler cannot widen the mouth.

paras: A clinician injects it in a short visit with results visible straight away, and swelling settles over days. It lasts months and people repeat it to maintain, often starting with a small amount and adding over time.

Swelling and bruising commonly last up to a week. Reviewers of lip safety describe complications that can be severe, note they are underreported, and say prospective randomised safety trials are lacking. Overfilling can look unnatural, and HA filler can be dissolved if needed.

social.title: Show HN: Lips Up – Preview lip filler on your own face

angle.text: Lip filler adds volume, defines the lip border and balances upper and lower lip, with the change visible straight away. It is temporary and well documented in trials; some forum rating systems weigh mouth width more heavily than lip fullness.

lead: Lip filler, or lip augmentation with fillers, is the injection of a soft-tissue filler, most commonly a hyaluronic acid (HA) gel, to increase lip volume, sharpen the vermilion border or improve the ratio between the upper and lower lip [1][2]. People use it to get fuller, more defined lips, to restore volume that has thinned with age, or to balance the lips against the nose and chin in the lower face. Perioral tissues are among the first to show ageing, and reviews say many patients seek perioral fillers as their first cosmetic treatment [3].

Reviews describe HA fillers as the gold standard for lip augmentation because they are biocompatible and reversible [4]. Randomized, multicenter trials have compared HA gels with each other, including a head-to-head comparison of four products [5][6]. Fat transfer and surgical approaches such as the lip lift are alternative methods [7][8].

A review of lip-filler safety states that the results are impressive but so are the reported complications, that there is a paucity of prospective randomized trials on safety, and that complications are under-reported [9]. In looksmaxxing communities lip filler is discussed as a small, accessible modification, alongside views that proportions of mouth to nose matter more than lip volume [10]. Many people come to it through the wider story of how HA moved from a food and joint-medicine ingredient into facial aesthetics from the 1990s, and through a 2015 celebrity episode that put lip augmentation in front of a mass audience [11][12].
infobox: Injectable soft-tissue filler, usually hyaluronic acid [4]
Varies by product; Restylane about six months, some HA claims up to 1 to 1.5 years [13]
HA fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase [4]
Fat transfer, lip lift, other fillers [7][8][13]
Medical device given by licensed clinicians (US) [28]
Hyaluronidase enzyme breaks down HA filler [21]

paras: Reviews describe lip anatomy in layers of skin, muscle and mucosa, with age-related volume loss, thinning of the vermilion border and flattening of the philtrum, and say treatment should be tailored to the individual, including ethnic differences in lip structure and cultural preferences [4]. Injection techniques include needles and cannulas, with attention to the vascular supply of the lips [4][1]. Perioral fillers can also be applied to the philtral columns, oral commissures and surrounding folds [3].

Wikipedia lists the materials that have been used in lips over time: autologous dermal material that is absorbed quickly, bovine collagen (needing a skin test and lasting about four weeks to three months), processed donor dermis placed along the vermilion, calcium hydroxylapatite gel (average about two years in one description), Gore-Tex implants, fat transfer, and permanent PMMA microsphere fillers that are not used in the lip body because they can show through thin skin and have caused nodules at the lip edge [13]. It describes fat transfer as rated by several studies as one of the better options for a semi-permanent, softer, fuller lip, and notes that tiny 30 to 31 gauge needles and topical anaesthetics have reduced discomfort since 2000 [13]. Non-surgical alternatives it names include lip plumpers containing irritants such as capsaicin and suction pumps, both of which cause temporary swelling [13].

A 2022 review of the lip lift, a surgical alternative, notes that a feminine lip has a shorter distance between the nasal sill and the vermilion border, fullness of the vermilion and a few millimetres of tooth show with the mouth slightly open, and that the lift is designed around natural anatomy [8].

According to Wikipedia, surgeons tried injecting paraffin into the lips around 1900 without success, liquid silicone was used from the early 1960s and abandoned about thirty years later over safety and appearance concerns, injectable bovine collagen became the standard around 1980, and newer products appeared after 2000 [13]. The shift since then has been toward HA fillers such as Restylane and Juvederm [13].

Wikipedia adds that growing demand for cosmetic procedures in the late 1990s brought more biocompatible materials into use, and that injection with very fine needles was a post-2000 refinement [13]. Early clinical work on non-animal stabilised HA includes a clinical and histological study of Restylane, a 2001 review of adverse reactions and skin testing for HA fillers, and a 2005 clinical comparison of injectable fillers for facial volume [14][15][16]. A 2008 review covered Juvederm for wrinkles and folds [17].

The filler in most lip treatments is hyaluronic acid, a sugar-chain molecule found naturally in skin. Wikipedia notes that natural HA is broken down by the body in about half a day, so manufacturers chemically cross-link the chains into a gel that persists longer after injection, and HA fillers are generally absorbed over roughly six to nine months [11]. Wikipedia's Restylane article calls Restylane, made by Galderma, the first HA filler approved by the US FDA for cosmetic injection into facial tissue, and says lip enhancement for volume and contouring is its most common use [18].

Wikipedia traces HA's path into aesthetics as follows: Karl Meyer and John Palmer at Columbia University first isolated it from cow eye in 1934, it was used in food and then in medicine for joints, wounds and eye surgery in the 1990s, it was first used for facial tissue augmentation in Europe in 1996, and the FDA approved Juvéderm in June 2006 on the basis of studies including a 146-person comparison with a collagen filler over 24 weeks [11]. A 2007 paper by Tom van Eijk in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology described a "fern pattern" placement technique for Restylane, an example of how injectors publish refinements to placement as well as product chemistry [18].

Different brands vary in how firm or soft the gel is, how much water it holds and how it is meant to be placed. Head-to-head trials compare these brands on lip fullness scales rather than declaring one best for every mouth [5][6][19][20].

A feature that distinguishes HA from older lip materials is that it can be broken down by the enzyme hyaluronidase. Wikipedia states that hyaluronidase can be injected to dissolve HA-type fillers and describes it as the best treatment option for dissolving lip filler or related complications, citing a 2022 scoping review [21]. A review of HA lip injections likewise lists reversibility as part of why HA is the preferred material [4]. This is a main reason people who want to try a fuller look treat HA as lower commitment than permanent materials; the same Wikipedia article on lip augmentation notes that permanent PMMA microspheres have caused nodules at the lip edge [13].

A 14-year analysis of procedure statistics from the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery covers trends in nonsurgical aesthetic procedures including fillers [22]. Trials of HA lip fillers typically assess lip fullness scales over months: a multicenter randomized double-blind study of 158 patients with thin lips compared a novel HA gel with a commercial comparator over six months [6], a non-inferiority randomized study tested a lidocaine-containing product [23], and an open-label randomized postmarket study followed another lidocaine product for short- and long-term safety [24]. The duration of results depends on the product, with HA fillers lasting roughly six months or longer according to Wikipedia [13].

The 2022 study of 158 patients with thin or very thin lips on a five-point Lip Fullness Grading Scale randomised them to a new HA gel or a commercial comparator, both with 0.3 percent lidocaine, and assessed efficacy over six months [6]. The head-to-head multicenter randomised, quadruple-blind comparison of four HA fillers was registered with 143 participants [5][19]. Registered studies include a long-term study of ART FILLER Volume and Lips (n=104), a study of a new filler for lip augmentation (n=273), a Saypha filler study (n=114), and a comparison of Emervel Lips with Juvederm Ultra Smile (n=40) [25][26][27][20].

Wikipedia lists redness, swelling and itching as common reactions and says swelling and bruising can last up to a week; other complications include bleeding, lumps, uneven lips and overfilling that appears unnatural [13]. Reviews of HA lip injections state that complications can be severe, and the authors emphasise anatomy knowledge and small aliquots of product to lower risk [9]. Across fillers, blindness from retrograde embolization is described as rare but usually permanent [28].

Wikipedia lists contraindications advised in descriptions of the procedure, including active cold sores, clotting disorders, infections, lip scarring and recurrent herpes simplex, and notes that smoking complicates healing and that some patients react to lidocaine [13]. Technique matters: overfilling can look unnatural, over-aggressive injection can cause lumpiness, and too little can leave ridges [13]. A 2001 JAAD article examined adverse reactions to HA skin fillers and the question of skin testing [15].

Human studies include randomized, multicenter trials comparing HA lip fillers with each other [5][6][23][24], a randomized trial comparing two upper lip augmentation approaches (V-Y technique versus micro-fat injection) on patient satisfaction [7], and reviews of technique and safety [1][9]. Registered trials include studies of four HA fillers [19], a new lip filler [25] and HA filler in ethnic lip augmentation [29].

Wikipedia's dermal filler article says the FDA regulates fillers as medical devices, with a provider prescribing and performing the injection, while in the UK and EEA fillers are non-prescription medical devices that need a CE mark, which confirms manufacturing standards but not medical efficacy [28]. It cites a review reporting that around 2010 more than 140 injectable fillers were on the UK and European market against only six approved in the US [28]. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons describes dermal fillers as a clinician-administered treatment [30].

Because rare vascular events such as blockage of a blood vessel are the most serious complication, reviews stress anatomical knowledge and small product amounts [9][28]. The T Nation posters quoted elsewhere in this article make a related observation: that the outcome depends heavily on who performs the injection [31][32].

Overfilled lips are mocked in the media as a "trout pout," a look that appears in tabloids, according to Wikipedia, and the same article says the result depends heavily on the provider's skill and experience [13]. A 14-year analysis by the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery tracks trends in surgical and nonsurgical aesthetic procedures, including fillers, worldwide [22]. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons lists plumping thin lips among the uses of dermal fillers and notes that fillers are temporary, with labelled durations of roughly six to twelve months or longer [30].

On T Nation, which is mainly a training forum, filler comes up in side discussion. One poster says people notice bad cosmetic work and then assume all of it looks bad, and another describes a cosmetic dermatologist's view that filler injections by non-specialists often give poor outcomes [31][32].

Wikipedia's Kylie Jenner biography records that she had said she only used lip liner and overlined her lips until a May 2015 episode of Keeping Up with the Kardashians showed her acknowledging lip filler [12]. In April 2015 a social-media trend dubbed the "Kylie Jenner Challenge" had people suctioning their lips into small glasses to swell them temporarily, with no indication that Jenner herself used the method; Wikipedia's lip augmentation article lists suction pumps among non-surgical plumping methods that cause temporary swelling [12][13]. Jenner said she was not trying to encourage young girls to look like her [12]. The article reports that her lips drew speculation and publicity but does not report a measured change in filler demand [12].
Tabloid shorthand such as "trout pout" for overfilled lips is documented on Wikipedia [13], and it is the counterpart of the interest in natural-looking results that practitioners stress.

On looksmax.org, one thread asks how common lip-filler complications are and whether an allergy test exists, with the poster saying thin lips are a major perceived flaw; replies range from the view that fillers are 'cope' because mouth width relative to nose width matters, to advice to see a plastic surgeon and that the amount used is small and cheap [10].

Other looksmax.org threads ask whether filler or lateral commissuroplasty is better for lip widening. One reply says filler cannot really widen lips and that lateral commissuroplasty adds only a few millimetres and risks scarring, while the poster says even a few millimetres would matter [33]. Other threads discuss upper-lip filler for projection and ways to add lower-lip volume without filler [34][35].

lore.intro: Lip filler is treated as an accessible way to address thin lips, but forum users dispute how much it matters relative to facial proportions [10].

claims.claim: Fuller lips are a cheap, easy improvement.
Lip filler is cope; mouth width relative to nose width matters more.
Lip filler can be undone if you dislike it.
Results depend more on who injects than on the product.
Celebrity culture drove the lip-filler boom.
